dimensions.note: No secrets. standInAgent names a behavior; the README says an agent that reads a vault needs that vault granted to app users, as a run's vault use is checked against who started it.
app_stand_in logs which stand-in takes its turn on which request after which step, or that none does; the nested turn logs as capture-stand-in always has.

A failed or missing decision fails closed: the guard errors or the nested step is skipped, and no turn runs. The app reports the step as taken once it is, even if deciding on a stand-in fails, and reports the step's own refusal otherwise.

78 tests pass. New ones cover who comes in and on which point after submit and reply, none on a draft, after steps Slack doesn't follow, with no agent, with two people or for an unknown login; and the app's step outcome from run events (done before the turn, the step's refusal, a failed decision, a nested run's events). Round 1 found the event handling untested; it is now a pure module with tests. Checked by hand under swamp serve with a fake 20s agent: the turn ran nested with only run on capture-app-step, and the app said Posted. in 1s.
A step that fails brings in no turn. As the README now says, nothing stops two quick steps each bringing in a turn, where Slack holds one per request in memory.
The nested run gets only app_stand_in's outputs: the agent from standInAgent and the stand-in from the people list, never from the app. The child checks the turn again (requireStandInTurn).

The app stops following once the step is taken; the run goes on. Round 1 found the maxWallClock comment implied a limit swamp doesn't apply; it now says serve's --max-run-duration bounds the turn, as the README does.

Round 1 found the README silent on how the app differs from Slack; it now says revisions and failed router tests bring in no turn, two turns can overlap, and the first stand-in by email is taken. A misplaced doc comment was fixed and standInNext added to the Output list.
Round 1 found a whitespace-only standInAgent counted as set; it is now trimmed. app_stand_in's step is the step enum and id is capped.
standInNext is kept 1d with GC 5; it is read in the same run.
It writes one decision record per step; nothing to update or delete.

Before deciding: the login is on the list, the request is readable to them and open, one person holds both roles, an agent is set and a stand-in exists for the role; it runs only after the step succeeded.
stand-in-next-<request id>, or -none for whoami and raise; a step reads its own run's output, so overlapping runs don't read each other's.
The request is read through the same visibility check as every step; nothing is written but the decision, and the turn's writes are the stand-in's, through Capture's rules.
Manifest and all three behavior types at 2026.11.27.2 with identity upgrades; standInAgent defaults to blank, so existing instances keep working and bring in no stand-in.
